title: Retrieval lab: name the failed boundary before changing the pipeline
goal: Diagnose five look-alike order-pipeline incidents, then choose a product-specific observation and a safe first action.
tag: Certification retrieval + gap check · cycle 3, position 7
concept:
A parcel disappears. Replacing the truck will not help if the real problem is a locked loading dock, a rejected label, the wrong customer shelf, an expired tracking bookmark, or a test copy that still depends on the original box.

Data incidents often look alike from the dashboard. Diagnose the boundary that stopped preserving truth before changing pipeline code: identity, schema, row policy, change position, or clone dependency.
example:
The same synthetic order O-42 from Day36 now produces one of five symptoms. An S3 read returns access denied. A new coupon_code is absent from the published table. Tenant beta can see an acme row. Fulfillment misses changes after downtime. A QA clone fails after source files or policy dependencies change.

Each symptom points to a different first inspection. A retry is useful only after the failed boundary is known.

use_case.when: Use this retrieval map during incident triage, certification practice, design reviews, and post-release checks for governed incremental pipelines.
use_case.example: An on-call engineer sees missing fulfillment updates after a weekend outage and must decide whether to inspect cloud access, schema rescue data, tenant policy, the change cursor, or clone dependencies.
use_case.decision: Start with the earliest boundary whose evidence contradicts the expected state. Collect read-only evidence first. Do not infer a personal knowledge gap from this generated exercise; use submitted answers and authorized product labs to decide what needs more study.

practice: Choose a symptom, predict the broken boundary, then reveal the safest first observation. Notice that retrying is never the first universal answer.
boundary: This local JavaScript teaching model maps five synthetic symptoms to likely first inspections. It does not run AWS, Databricks, or Snowflake, prove root cause, inspect logs, test privileges, recover expired history, validate policy semantics, or establish certification mastery. Vendor SQL/PySpark is sourced but unexecuted.

symptom
'+incidentSymptom.options[incidentSymptom.selectedIndex].text+'
likely boundary
'+boundary+'
first observation
'+action+'
';};incidentSymptom.onchange=paintTriage;paintTriage();
questions: Changes disappear only after a long outage. Which evidence is most useful first?
The durable cursor and retained change-history window
The clone name
The number of columns
The symptom is about an incremental position crossing a retention boundary.
Why inspect evidence before retrying?
A retry can repeat the same failure or hide the boundary that lost truth
Retries repair every policy
Retries recreate expired history
A retry is an action, not a diagnosis.
What does this retrieval session establish about your readiness?
Only delivered practice; mastery still needs answers and real product evidence
A passing certification result
Complete COF-C03 coverage
Generated curriculum coverage and personal mastery are separate.

product_sections.title: Databricks retrieval: separate access, schema, policy, cursor, and clone evidence
product_sections.html:
One incident, five evidence locations. Access denial starts at the storage credential and external-location path. A missing field starts at Auto Loader schema history and rescued data. Wrong rows start at the effective identity and row filter. Missing changes start at the CDF starting version and checkpoint. A broken shallow clone starts at its source-file dependency.

Failure/fix. If the requested CDF history is gone, a retry cannot recreate it. Reconcile from an authoritative snapshot or other retained source, reset the consumer position deliberately, and document the gap. If automatic CDF conflicts with row filters, split the internal change surface from filtered serving.

product_sections.title: Snowflake retrieval: read the Stream clock and policy context before recreating anything
product_sections.html:
Start with the Stream state. A Stream becomes stale when its offset falls outside retained history. SHOW STREAMS exposes STALE and STALE_AFTER. Recreating the Stream resumes future tracking; it does not by itself recover the missed interval. Wrong row visibility is a separate policy-context problem. A clone can also have policy references or historical-change boundaries that differ from the source.

-- sourced diagnostic sketches; not executed hereSHOW STREAMS LIKE 'ORDERS_DELTA';SELECT SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA('ORDERS_DELTA');-- reconcile missed rows before CREATE OR REPLACE STREAM

Failure/fix. Consume before STALE_AFTER and monitor the clock. After staleness, preserve the gap question, reconcile from retained authoritative data where possible, then recreate the Stream for future changes.

title: computeIfAbsent is atomic; the loader must still be short
goal: Use ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent for small atomic initialization without turning a map bin into a slow remote-call queue.
concept:
A coat-check clerk can assign one hook number atomically. If the clerk leaves the desk for an eight-second phone call while holding the assignment book, other updates may wait.

ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent performs the invocation atomically for an absent key. Oracle documents that some attempted updates may block while the function runs, so the mapping function should be short and simple and must not update the same map.
example: Two requests miss tenant acme at the same time. A fast mapping creates an empty PolicyHolder; asynchronous refresh fills it later. A slow mapping that calls a policy service for 800 ms can make unrelated updates contend and makes failure handling live inside an atomic map operation.

use_case.when: Use computeIfAbsent for cheap construction such as a local holder, counter, lock, or memoized value with bounded computation.
use_case.example: Create one per-tenant circuit-breaker holder atomically, then let the holder manage remote refresh outside the map computation.
use_case.decision: Keep the mapping pure, short, and non-recursive. For slow I/O, store a promise/holder deliberately or use a cache library with explicit loading, expiry, failure, and refresh behavior.

practice: Change loader duration and whether it performs remote I/O. Watch the single absent-key lane become a waiting line.
boundary: The browser uses a deterministic wait arithmetic model. It does not run threads, model ConcurrentHashMap bin structure, scheduler timing, exceptions, null returns, cache eviction, stampedes after failure, visibility beyond documented map guarantees, or prove throughput. The Java replay only executes one local map initialization.

function paintMap(){const ms=+mapLoadMs.value,slow=remoteLoad.checked||ms>50;mapWorld.innerHTML='
two misses
key acme
atomic mapping
'+ms+' ms
second updater
'+(slow?'may wait':'quickly observes holder')+'
';};mapLoadMs.oninput=paintMap;remoteLoad.onchange=paintMap;paintMap();
questions: The mapping function calls a remote service for 800 ms. Main risk?
Other attempted updates may block while the atomic computation runs
The value is inserted twice by definition
ConcurrentHashMap becomes a HashMap
Atomicity does not make slow work cheap.
Why create a small holder in the mapping function?
It keeps atomic initialization short while moving lifecycle work elsewhere
It disables concurrency
It guarantees cache eviction
Separate map publication from remote loading policy.
What must the mapping function avoid?
Recursive updates to the same map
Returning a local object
Reading its key
The documented contract forbids modifying the map during computation.

steps.note: Create a thread-safe map.
Atomically install one small local value.
The second call observes the existing mapping.
Record the local result; this does not benchmark contention.

walkthrough.limit: The browser uses a deterministic wait arithmetic model. It does not run threads, model ConcurrentHashMap bin structure, scheduler timing, exceptions, null returns, cache eviction, stampedes after failure, visibility beyond documented map guarantees, or prove throughput. The Java replay only executes one local map initialization.

visual_explanation: The single-key lane shows why an atomic function can become a queue. The waiting updater changes state when the mapping crosses the declared short-work threshold or performs remote I/O.
written_questions: Which computeIfAbsent functions in your services perform I/O, logging, or recursive cache access?
Design a holder or explicit loader that keeps publication short without hiding refresh failures.

title: Match decision process to reversal cost
goal: Use a light, local experiment for reversible choices and deeper review for choices whose rollback is slow or harmful.
concept:
Choosing a movable whiteboard does not need the same committee as cutting a load-bearing wall. The first is easy to undo; the second is not.

Amazon describes reversible choices as two-way doors and difficult-to-reverse choices as one-way doors. The engineering move is to make reversibility concrete: rollback time, customer blast radius, data migration cost, and contract commitments.
example: Changing an internal dashboard color behind a flag is a two-way door. Repartitioning 10 PB while deleting the old layout, changing a public event schema without dual-read support, or selecting an irreversible vendor data format moves toward a one-way door.

use_case.when: Use a reversibility check when architecture reviews, standards, migrations, or platform choices are either moving too slowly or moving with hidden lock-in.
use_case.example: A team wants a six-week review for a feature-flagged library trial but only a short meeting for a destructive table migration.
use_case.decision: Write the rollback path first. Delegate reversible experiments with guardrails and evidence. Add review depth, staged migration, and explicit ownership as rollback time, irreversible data change, or cross-team blast radius grows.

practice: Change rollback time, blast radius, and whether old data remains. Watch the decision move between team experiment, architecture review, and executive risk acceptance.
boundary: This is a judgment aid, not an organizational approval policy. It does not price legal, regulatory, vendor, security, or reputation risk; decide thresholds locally and keep emergency authority explicit.
js:
function paintDoor(){const hard=+rollbackHours.value>24||+blastTeams.value>5||!oldPathKept.checked;doorWorld.innerHTML='
rollback '+rollbackHours.value+' h
'+blastTeams.value+' teams
old path '+(oldPathKept.checked?'kept':'removed')+'
'+(hard?'methodical review':'local guarded experiment')+'
';};[rollbackHours,blastTeams].forEach(x=>x.oninput=paintDoor);oldPathKept.onchange=paintDoor;paintDoor();

A local guarded experiment with evidence

What makes a data migration less reversible?
Deleting the old representation before validation and rollback windows close
Writing an ADR
Using a dashboard
The rollback path must survive long enough to be real.
Why classify reversibility explicitly?
To spend review depth where a wrong choice is hardest to undo
To avoid all architecture review
To guarantee the decision is correct
The model improves decision-process fit, not certainty.

steps.note: Apply a declared teaching threshold.

title: Approval allows a tool call; an idempotency key prevents duplicate effects
goal: Carry one stable logical-action key through retries so an approved side effect is applied once at the destination.
concept:
A manager signs one payment form. A courier delivers the same signed form twice after a network retry. The signature authorizes the payment; it does not tell the bank whether this is a duplicate delivery.

Human approval and idempotency solve different problems. Approval answers “may this exact action run?” A stable idempotency key lets the destination atomically recognize repeated delivery of the same logical action.
example: An agent proposes refund order O-42 for $25. The human approves those exact arguments. The harness sends key refund:O-42:v1. A timeout causes the same request to be retried with the same key and parameters. The refund service returns the stored result instead of issuing a second refund.

use_case.when: Use stable action keys for approved payments, refunds, ticket creation, email sends, infrastructure mutations, and any tool that can be retried after an ambiguous timeout.
use_case.example: A refund tool times out after the payment processor committed the refund but before the agent received the response.
use_case.decision: Bind approval to exact arguments, derive or persist one logical-action key, reuse both across retries, and let the destination atomically store the first outcome. If the destination has no idempotency contract, treat ambiguous timeouts as reconciliation work, not safe automatic retry.

practice: Choose whether the retry reuses the key and whether parameters changed. Watch authorization and duplicate-effect protection fail independently.
boundary: The browser models a set of seen keys. It does not run an agent, authenticate a user, persist approvals, define key-retention windows, prevent malicious key reuse, reconcile partial external effects, or prove a destination implements atomic idempotency.
js:
function paintIdempotency(){const allowed=toolApproved.checked&&sameArguments.checked,duplicate=allowed&&reuseActionKey.checked;idempotencyWorld.innerHTML='
approval '+(toolApproved.checked?'present':'missing')+'
arguments '+(sameArguments.checked?'match':'changed')+'
retry key '+(reuseActionKey.checked?'stable':'new')+'
'+(!allowed?'do not execute':duplicate?'one refund result':'duplicate refund risk')+'
';};[toolApproved,reuseActionKey,sameArguments].forEach(x=>x.onchange=paintIdempotency);paintIdempotency();

Only with the same approved arguments and a destination-enforced stable idempotency key

Retry changes $25 to $30 but keeps the old key. What now?
Reject and seek a new approval/logical action

The key must remain bound to the same logical action and parameters.

Stop automatic replay and reconcile the external state
Generate random keys until one works
Repeat the approval text
Without atomic destination deduplication, the effect is uncertain.

The first delivery records key and effect together in the teaching model.

steps.note: The retry finds the same key and returns the prior outcome.

walkthrough.limit: The browser models a set of seen keys. It does not run an agent, authenticate a user, persist approvals, define key-retention windows, prevent malicious key reuse, reconcile partial external effects, or prove a destination implements atomic idempotency.

visual_explanation: The four independent gates show that approval, argument binding, stable retry identity, and destination deduplication are separate. Turning off only key reuse keeps authorization green while exposing a duplicate-effect risk.
written_questions: Which agent tools can cross an ambiguous timeout after committing a side effect?
Where will the stable key and first result be stored atomically, and how long must that record live?

title: A helical molecule can turn current into one-way rotation
goal: Trace how voltage polarity, a rotation threshold, and molecular shape connect direction of motion to higher conductance in a new prototype.
concept:
An Archimedes screw turns in one direction to move water. Shrink the spiral down to one molecule and replace flowing water with electric current.

Researchers suspended a helical organic molecule between two gold electrode tips. Applied voltage produced cyclic motion with reported 100% directional preference; reversing voltage polarity reversed direction. Above a threshold, calculations and measurements linked rotation to access to higher-conductance configurations.
example: Use normalized voltage rather than claiming the experiment's exact operating value. At +0.8, the toy rotor stays below threshold. At +1.2, it rotates forward and enters an enhanced-conductance state. At -1.2, direction reverses while the magnitude remains above threshold.

use_case.when: Use this research when studying molecular machines, current-induced forces, or future single-molecule electronic components.
use_case.example: A laboratory prototype explores whether a single molecular junction can couple directional mechanical motion to an electrically readable conductance change.
use_case.decision: Treat it as early-stage physics, not a production motor or transistor. Practical use needs room-temperature operation, repeatable fabrication, lifetime, control, scaling, and device-integration evidence.

practice: Change normalized voltage polarity and molecular compression. Predict direction and whether the threshold is crossed before reading the state.
boundary: This is an original normalized threshold model, not the paper's quantum-transport or molecular-dynamics calculation. It does not reproduce voltage, temperature, conductance magnitude, gold-tip geometry, stochastic jumps, friction, stretching forces, device lifetime, or fabrication variability.
js:
function paintMolecule(){const v=+moleculeVoltage.value/10,threshold=1+(+moleculeCompression.value/10),rotates=Math.abs(v)>=threshold,dir=v>0?'forward':v<0?'reverse':'none';moleculeWorld.innerHTML='
polarity '+(v>0?'+':v<0?'-':'0')+'
|V| '+Math.abs(v).toFixed(1)+' vs threshold '+threshold.toFixed(1)+'
rotation '+(rotates?dir:'stepwise / below toy threshold')+'
conductance '+(rotates?'enhanced state':'rest-state range')+'
';};[moleculeVoltage,moleculeCompression].forEach(x=>x.oninput=paintMolecule);paintMolecule();

Rotation direction reverses and the enhanced state remains available

A commercial molecular motor

Which boundary matters most for application claims?
Fabrication, temperature, lifetime, control, and scaling remain open
A normalized slider proves the mechanism

A single-junction experiment does not establish engineering readiness.

steps.note: Use a normalized positive voltage.
Declare a teaching threshold rather than an experimental value.

steps.code: rotates = abs(voltage) >= threshold; direction = 'forward' if voltage > 0 else 'reverse'
steps.note: Magnitude crosses the threshold; polarity selects direction.
Connect rotation to the qualitative conductance state.

It does not reproduce voltage, temperature, conductance magnitude, gold-tip geometry, stochastic jumps, friction, stretching forces, device lifetime, or fabrication variability.

What evidence would be required before calling this a usable molecular electronic component?

title: One deployment at a time is not a rollback
goal: Use a concurrency group to prevent overlap while keeping cancellation and production recovery as separate designs.
concept:
A one-lane bridge prevents two trucks from colliding. It does not tow the first truck back if its engine fails halfway across.

A GitHub Actions concurrency group can limit overlapping production jobs. cancel-in-progress can cancel an older run, but cancellation of workflow steps does not guarantee reversal of external effects already applied to Kubernetes, Databricks, or another target.
example: Run A starts deploying image v2. Run B for v3 arrives. With cancellation enabled, GitHub stops A's remaining steps. If A already changed half the services, production is mixed until an explicit rollback or a safe v3 reconciliation completes.

use_case.when: Use deployment concurrency when two releases to the same environment could race, overwrite state, or produce confusing approval and observability signals.
use_case.example: Two merges trigger production updates to the same EKS namespace or Databricks job bundle within one minute.
use_case.decision: Give each target environment a stable concurrency key. Queue when every release must run; cancel only when deployment steps are interruption-safe or reconciliatory. Design rollback, health checks, and artifact identity separately.

practice: Choose queue or cancel, then move Run A past its external side effect. Watch cancellation stop workflow execution without undoing production.
boundary: The model shows two runs and one external flag. It does not call GitHub, guarantee queue order, model multiple pending runs, environment protection, reusable workflows, signal handling, cloud deployment semantics, rollback automation, or runner termination timing.

function paintDeploy(){const cancel=deployPolicy.value==='cancel',changed=externalChanged.checked;deployWorld.innerHTML='
Run A '+(cancel?'canceled':'continues')+'
production '+(changed?'already changed':'unchanged')+'
Run B '+(cancel?'can start':'waits')+'
rollback '+(changed?'still required / reconcile':'not needed yet')+'
';};deployPolicy.onchange=paintDeploy;externalChanged.onchange=paintDeploy;paintDeploy();

title: 202 Accepted means queued, not completed
goal: Return an explicit status monitor for asynchronous work and make clients handle eventual failure instead of treating 202 as business success.
concept:
A repair shop says, “We accepted your car.” That does not mean the repair passed inspection.

HTTP 202 Accepted means processing was accepted but has not completed and might not ultimately happen. RFC 9110 says the response ought to describe current status and point to or embed a status monitor.
example: POST /exports returns 202 with job exp-42 and /exports/exp-42. The worker later moves it from queued to running to succeeded or failed. The client polls the monitor and downloads only after success.

use_case.when: Use 202 when work cannot finish within the request latency budget and completion will happen in a separate worker or batch process.
use_case.example: A user starts a 200 GB governed export, backfill, model build, or cross-region copy that may take minutes.
use_case.decision: Use synchronous 200/201 when work is complete. For 202, return a durable job identity, status monitor, failure details, retry guidance, and idempotent submission behavior. Do not use 202 merely to hide overload.

practice: Move exp-42 through queued, running, failed, and succeeded. Watch which client action is safe at each state.
boundary: The model uses one in-memory job. It does not run HTTP, define a standard status-monitor header, persist jobs, authenticate monitor access, guarantee delivery, model webhooks, retries, cancellation, expiry, idempotency keys, rate limits, or RFC-compliant response bodies.

function paintAccepted(){const s=jobState.value,done=s==='succeeded',failed=s==='failed';acceptedWorld.innerHTML='
POST /exports
202 + exp-42
GET /exports/exp-42
'+s+'
client '+(done?'downloads':failed?'shows failure':'waits / polls')+'
';};jobState.onchange=paintAccepted;paintAccepted();

walkthrough.limit: The model uses one in-memory job. It does not run HTTP, define a standard status-monitor header, persist jobs, authenticate monitor access, guarantee delivery, model webhooks, retries, cancellation, expiry, idempotency keys, rate limits, or RFC-compliant response bodies.

How will clients safely retry the initial submission without creating a second job?
